questions.prompt: What do Fern and Dewdrop find at the source of the silent stream?
choices: A great boulder lay across the singing stones.
The singing stones had floated downstream.
A fallen tree had dried up all the water.
questions.answer: A great boulder lay across the singing stones.
questions.evidenceText:
A great boulder had fallen.
It lay across the singing stones.

questions.prompt: How did Fern and Dewdrop combine their abilities to free the stones?
choices: Fern grew a vine around the boulder while Dewdrop sent water under it.
Fern sang to the boulder while Dewdrop carried it away.
Fern dug a tunnel while Dewdrop froze the rock.
questions.answer: Fern grew a vine around the boulder while Dewdrop sent water under it.
questions.evidenceText:
Fern grew a strong vine around the boulder.
Dewdrop sent water under it to loosen the mud.

questions.prompt: What lesson does Fern understand before they move the boulder?
choices: Some problems are easier when friends work together.
Dewdrop's water was strong enough to move it alone.
Fern's vine moved the boulder without any water.
questions.answer: Some problems are easier when friends work together.
questions.rationale: Fern says they need each other, then Fern's vine and Dewdrop's water work together to move the boulder; this shows some problems are easier when friends work together.

supportingEvidence.evidenceText:
Fern grew a strong vine around the boulder.
Dewdrop sent water under it to loosen the mud.

They pushed and pulled together.
The boulder shifted.
The mud let go.
The boulder rolled aside.
